title: Images need alternative text
summary: An image has no alt attribute, so screen readers skip it or read out the file name. Add alt text that says what the image shows or does.
problem: An element has no alt attribute. Without it, a screen reader has nothing useful to announce, so it often reads the file name aloud (something like "IMG_4021.jpg") or skips the image altogether.
whoItAffects: People who are blind or have low vision and use a screen reader never learn what the image shows, whether that is a product photo, a chart or an icon that works as a button. The same text appears when an image fails to load, and search engines read it to understand what the image is.
steps: Find the image in your theme, template or CMS. The scan result shows the exact markup.
If the image carries information, or sits inside a link or button, add a short alt phrase that says what it shows or where it leads, such as alt="Navy cotton shirt, front view".
If the image is purely decorative, add an empty alt (alt="") so screen readers skip it. Leaving the attribute off is not the same thing.
Leave out phrases like "image of" or "photo of". Screen readers already announce that it is an image.
For charts and diagrams, put the main takeaway in the alt text and give the full data in nearby text or a table.
whyItMatters: A shopper who cannot see your product photos has no way to tell what you sell, so they leave. Missing alt text is a failure of WCAG 1.1.1 at Level A, the baseline that accessibility laws and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Open your browser's accessibility inspector, select the image, and read its Name. An empty Name means the alt text is missing. A screen reader such as VoiceOver or NVDA will show you the same thing in practice.

platformNotes.note: Open the image in the Media Library and fill in the Alternative Text field. Images added in theme code need the alt attribute added to the template.
In the product editor, click the image and choose Add alt text. For images in theme files, set the alt attribute in the Liquid template.
